title: Displayed Horizontal Word List

illustrates.quote: Format for Displayed Short Word Lists. Horizontal word lists across the print page must fit on a single braille line, with each word separated by a blank cell. (See UEB, §3.23.1, Space.) Present phrases vertically. The first word begins at the adjusted left margin.

blocks.text: Suppose you are asked to arrange the following words into a sentence.

blocks.features: Three single words displayed horizontally in bold on one print line, fitting on a single braille line with one blank cell between each, per 9.2.4.

blocks.text: There is more than one sentence that can be made from these words.

print.notes: Direct worked example of 9.2.4: the three-word horizontal list fits on one braille line, each word separated by exactly one blank cell (U+2800 in the source .txt, converted to a single space), beginning at the adjusted left margin (cell 3).
print.printFeatures: Plain (unboxed) worked-example text; the three list words are bold in print.

The word-list line's own inter-word separators are literal blank braille cells in the source (U+2800), not page-margin filler, converted to single ASCII spaces per the 'blank cells as spaces' convention.

resolution: A and B transcribed identical `braille.lines` and agreed the rule illustrated is 9.2.4; both verified independently byte-for-byte against lines 6665-6671 after stripping the measured 8-space margin. No disagreement to resolve.
